items.title: It's Official: Clair Obscur Will Never Be The Same
items.summary: It's officially the end of an era for the Clair Obscur franchise, and its future is now uncertain.
items.content:
Lune holding a glowing object while looking surprised in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Nicholas Becher Published Nov 17, 2026, 9:33 PM EST Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Most-played games range from Clair Obscur to Civ to Elden Ring to Halo 2 and beyond. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There's been a major development behind the scenes at Sandfall Interactive, the studio behind the award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , and the future of the franchise will officially never be the same. Sandfall Interactive and the idea behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 started from extremely humble beginnings. Before there was even a proper studio, two Ubisoft developers and a writer were already shaping what would eventually become one of gaming's biggest breakout hits.

Their ambitious vision for a story-driven RPG gradually evolved into a global phenomenon, with Expedition 33 earning hundreds of awards including GOTY and widespread acclaim for its memorable characters, heartbreaking story, and innovative gameplay. That extraordinary success has raised expectations for a Clair Obscur sequel or follow-up project through the roof.

However, in a new interview with Games Beat , lead writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has officially confirmed her departure from Sandfall Interactive, marking a major turning point for the franchise.

In a November 17 interview with Dean Takahashi, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she departed Sandfall Interactive back in July 2026, several months before the news became public. When asked whether she was still involved with the studio in any capacity, the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 lead writer gave a very blunt answer:

"I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We’ve parted ways."

The announcement came during a much broader conversation about Svedberg-Yen's future, following her selection for BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. recognition. She explained that she's working to establish a narrative investment fund designed to help smaller game developers secure early funding, while encouraging studios to prioritize storytelling throughout the development process.

That philosophy played an enormous role in Expedition 33 's creation. Svedberg-Yen was involved before Sandfall had even formally been established, joining two Ubisoft developers in April 2020 as the team's third member. She helped develop the game's original premise and themes, explaining that "Narrative is king" was an important part of the studio's approach from the beginning.

Close window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-17852177"] = '" Close "'; Looking back, she spoke highly of the collaboration between Sandfall's various creative departments and said she was especially proud of how strongly the characters connected with players. The way fans responded to the game's themes of grief, and the personal conversations it inspired, had an impact she never anticipated.

Beyond her planned investment fund, Svedberg-Yen also revealed that she's developing two personal storytelling projects, one intended for television and another for film, both incorporating gaming elements. She also emphasized that her biggest priority is helping the gaming industry support its creative talent, particularly younger developers struggling to break into the business.

While she didn't provide a detailed explanation for her departure or suggest that the split was acrimonious, it's undoubtedly a significant loss for Sandfall. With its original narrative lead no longer at the studio, any future Clair Obscur installment will have to move forward without one of the key creative minds who helped define Expedition 33 's award-winning storytelling.

items.title: Clair Obscur writer will invest in next generation of game storytellers | Jennifer Svedberg-Yen interview
items.summary: Hollywood & Games returns to Los Angeles on December 10, bringing together 250+ executives, founders, investors and decision-makers at the Grammy Museum's Clive Davis...
items.content:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen , the narrative lead for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award, and she’s using the win to draw attention to a new fund for narrative leads in games.

This comes after she scored a big win on Clair Obscur — her first game as a narrative designer and writer after a career in private equity — a game with a strong narrative that won more than 400 awards. And she is now using her financial expertise to set up a fund dedicated to advance the art of narrative design.

The goal is to create new funding models that could nurture talent, rather than extract from it. And too often people forget that strong stories in games from The Last of Us to Resident Evil are what makes the best games so memorable.

Svedberg-Yen is still adjusting to life after Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. She discovered she won the award while sitting in a bagel shop and puzzling over a mysterious calendar invite.

But while the recognition celebrates her work on Sandfall Interactive’s breakout hit, Svedberg-Yen is already looking toward a larger mission: helping reshape how the game industry develops stories and supports creative talent. She left Sandfall back in July to focus on her new mission.

Svedberg-Yen wants to make sure that narrative is considered at the outset when a game is created. She feels that it’s too often treated as an afterthought in game development.

After consulting with numerous studios, she said she repeatedly encountered teams that viewed story as either scriptwriting or a layer added after core gameplay is complete. In her experience, that approach limits what a game can become.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense. But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

That philosophy was embedded into Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 from the start in April 2020. Svedberg-Yen joined what would eventually become Sandfall Interactive before the studio formally existed. At the time, the team consisted of only two Ubisoft developers and herself.

Together they helped shape the game’s core concept and themes, making narrative a foundational pillar rather than an accessory.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game.”

Going forward, Svedberg-Yen wants to finish more of her own creative works, including stories intended for film and television, while continuing to explore ways to support fellow creators.

One of her techniques for writing is to have a rich life outside of work. If you get to know and observe people and hear their stories, you can walk in their shoes and have empathy for them.

“If you’re trying to write about people, you must understand people,” she said. “To understand people you need experience and empathy.”

items.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Star Connor Storrie, ‘Obsession’ Ingenue Inde Navarette and ‘Backrooms’ Filmmaker Kane Parsons Set as BAFTA U.S. Breakouts
items.summary: The organization revealed the roster of 14 "rising creatives" paving their way through film, television and games and "helping shape the future of the screen industries."
items.content:
BAFTA has blessed its breakthrough class of 2026.

The organization has revealed the roster of talent — actors and directors to writers and below-the-line standouts — selected to shine as its BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. cohort for the year. It’s a list of 14 “rising creatives” paving their way through film, television and games and “helping shape the future of the screen industries.”

The list (in alphabetical order by first names with mention of their breakout project) includes Union County filmmaker Adam Meeks, The Burbs creator Celeste Hughey, Heated Rivalry heartthrob Connor Storrie , Nuisance Bear documentary director Gabriela Osio Vanden, 1923 and Frisco King costume designer Gaby Acosta, Night Nurse filmmaker Georgia Bernstein, Obsession star Inde Navarrette , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 game lead writer and voice and localization producer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, Despelote game lead developer Julián Cordero, Backrooms filmmaker Kane Parsons , Bandi composer Marcus Norris, Barbara Forever documentary editor Matt Hixon, Bedford Park filmmaker Stephanie Ahn and South Midnight game writer Zaire Lanier. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV LGBTQ Representation on TV Dropped in 2025-26, GLAAD Study Finds Movies 'Wet,' Starring Connor Storrie, Rebecca Ferguson and Odessa A'zion, Acquired by Lionsgate

BAFTA Breakthrough, supported by Apple TV, is now in its seventh year. It’s described as the arts charity’s flagship talent initiative, and is designed to support creatives at a pivotal point in their careers. The cohort receives access to professional development, industry connections and opportunities to build their networks within the creative community. They take part in a year-long program, which features one-on-one meetings and career guidance, full BAFTA voting membership, access to BAFTA events and screenings and networking opportunities here and abroad. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“This year’s cohort reflects the imagination, ambition and distinct perspectives that continue to push our industries forward. At a time when emerging creatives face increasing challenges in finding opportunity, mentorship and a path forward, BAFTA is proud to create a space where talent can be recognized, supported and connected to a broader creative community,” explained BAFTA North America executive director Courtney LaBarge Bell. “Each member of this cohort brings a unique point of view and a commitment to their craft that we believe deserves to be seen and championed. Over the next year, we look forward to supporting their growth, creating meaningful connections and helping open doors as they continue to build lasting careers.”

The roster was selected by a jury that included Adolpho Veloso, Alysa Nahmias, Arseni Khachaturan, Julia Kim, Peter Teschner, Rolfe Kent, Sonia Kennebeck, Bella Gonzales and Nana Mensah for film and TV, and Bethany Higa, Bhamini Lakshminarayan, Del Walker, Mai Koythong, Michael Surya, Nick Apostolides, Robert Dominguez and Virginia Leo for games. Alums include Stephanie Economou, HIKARI, Nava Mau, Bao Nguyen, Fernando Reyes Medina, Karrie Shirou Shao, Erica Tremblay, Cheyenne Pualani Morrin, Sean Wang, Erika Ishii, Eva Victor and Chase Infiniti.

items.title: GTA 6 Will Never Be Able to Beat Clair Obscur at The Game Awards
items.summary: It's almost impossible for GTA 6 to get more nominations, and more wins will be very difficult
items.content:
By Oli Welsh Published Nov 17, 2026, 7:51 AM EST Oli Welsh has been covering the business and culture of video games for two decades. He started out writing for Edge and other publications (specializing in MMOs and Blizzard, as cover for his World of Warcraft playtime) before joining Eurogamer, where he worked for 14 years as reviews editor, deputy editor, and editor-in-chief; Eurogamer won many Games Media Awards during his tenure. At Polygon, he writes about film and TV as well as games, and provides news, analysis, and criticism on the entertainment we love and the industries that make it, all from his home in London. He loves role-playing, racing, puzzles, tactics, exploration, storytelling, Nintendo, mysteries, spies, fantasy, reality, cars, and classic cinema. He wanted to be a movie critic when he grew up, and now he’s definitely grown up, and occasionally is one. He considers this a win. GOTY Watch It's almost impossible for GTA 6 to get more nominations, and more wins will be very difficult

GTA6 Rockstar Games Official Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Grand Theft Auto 6 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The triumph of Grand Theft Auto 6 at this year's Game Awards has seemed inevitable all year — especially in the face of what has turned out to be relatively weak competition . So you might assume that it's going to break records as it sweeps the board, just as it's going to break records commercially. But you'd be wrong.

The records for most nominations and most wins were set last year by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Sandfall Interactive's RPG was nominated for 13 awards and won nine. It is practically, if not theoretically, impossible for GTA 6 to beat these totals.

Although the two games are very different, Clair Obscur was similarly dominant in the awards narrative. Like GTA 6 , nothing emerged all year that could realistically compete with it. And although it's a much smaller production, it excelled in the craft categories: performance, narrative, art direction, and music. It was nominated for, and won, most of the categories it was eligible for. The same looks likely to be true for GTA 6 . So how come it can't beat it?

Crucially, Clair Obscur was eligible for two categories where GTA 6 can't compete: Best Independent Game and Best Debut Indie Game. Some have quibbled with Clair Obscur 's definition as an indie, as it was a reasonably large-scale and well-funded production. But it was made by an independent studio for an indie-specialist publisher, so it's not an unreasonable definition. Either way, it happened.

Clair Obscur was nominated for Game of the Year, for all five craft categories (Game Direction, Narrative, Art Direction, Score and Music, Audio Design), and for the two indie categories. It had no less than three nominations in the Best Performance category (half the field). It was nominated for Best Role-Playing Game, its genre category. (Games can only be nominated in one genre category.) And it was nominated for the fan-voted Players' Voice award.

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Let's assume that GTA 6 matches Clair Obscur beat-for-beat across GOTY, the craft categories, its genre category (Best Action/Adventure Game, in this case), and in Players' Voice. That seems a pretty safe assumption. Even if it can match Clair Obscur 's three performance nominations (a tall order, since jury members haven't spent as long with the characters), it would have to make up those two indie categories somewhere else to equal Clair Obscur 's record.

After ruling out the other genres, there are only a few other categories still on the table where that would be possible. GTA 6 is ineligible for most of them: Best Multiplayer, Ongoing Game, Mobile Game, VR/AR Game, and Community Support (as an unreleased game, it currently has no actual community). It hardly seems likely to get picked for Best Family Game or Games for Impact (however worthy it may or may not be). That only leaves Innovation in Accessibility. I have no idea about GTA 6 's credentials in this field. It might be great, although, given its late release, it will be untested by the public.

Lucia Caminos GTA6 Rockstar Games So, in order to match Clair Obscur 's record (never mind beat it), GTA 6 would have to be nominated for the accessibility award and get an unprecedented four Performance nominations. It's theoretically possible, but incredibly unlikely. I see GTA 6 netting out at 9 or 10 nominations, depending on whether both of the actors playing Jason and Lucia get nominated (or perhaps one of them plus a character part, such as Stephen Root's Brian Heder).

It will also be very difficult for GTA 6 to beat Clair Obscur 's nine wins. Clair Obscur ran an almost perfect game, winning in every category it was nominated for but two: Audio Design and Players' Voice. GTA 6 would have to win every single category I see it being nominated in to match that. It would need to be nominated in, and win, Innovation in Accessibility to beat it.

Neither scenario is impossible, but both are highly unlikely. These are two records GTA 6 is not going to break. In fact, given the unique circumstances surrounding Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 — an indie game with AAA production values and a beloved cast of actors — I expect these records are going to stand for a long, long time.

The timing of Rockstar's entry into the 2026 GOTY race could scarcely be more awkward

items.title: The 2026 GOTY Race Could Be a Disaster for Indie Games
items.summary: After three indie nominees last year, this year’s leading contender is in trouble
items.content:
By Oli Welsh Published Nov 15, 2026, 12:00 PM EST Oli Welsh has been covering the business and culture of video games for two decades. He started out writing for Edge and other publications (specializing in MMOs and Blizzard, as cover for his World of Warcraft playtime) before joining Eurogamer, where he worked for 14 years as reviews editor, deputy editor, and editor-in-chief; Eurogamer won many Games Media Awards during his tenure. At Polygon, he writes about film and TV as well as games, and provides news, analysis, and criticism on the entertainment we love and the industries that make it, all from his home in London. He loves role-playing, racing, puzzles, tactics, exploration, storytelling, Nintendo, mysteries, spies, fantasy, reality, cars, and classic cinema. He wanted to be a movie critic when he grew up, and now he’s definitely grown up, and occasionally is one. He considers this a win. GOTY Watch After three indie nominees last year, this year’s leading contender is in trouble

Image: House House/Panic via Polygon Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Last year was a watershed moment for indie games at The Game Awards . Three games were nominated for both Game of the Year and Best Independent Game: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , Hades 2 , and Hollow Knight: Silksong . Together, they made up half of the GOTY 2025 field.

Some quibble with the definition of Clair Obscur , a sizable production, as an indie game. (For what it's worth, the studio that made it is independent, and its publisher Kepler Interactive was founded by a collective of indie studios; it's definitely culturally indie.) But even if you excluded it, this was still the first time more than one game had crossed over between the indie and GOTY categories in the history of the awards.

If you interpret this result as a sure sign that The Game Awards is taking indie games much more seriously, I'm afraid you might be disappointed. The 2025 nominations flatter to deceive, and 2026 looks like it will be a different matter. All three 2025 indie GOTY nominees were huge sellers, and two of them were high-profile sequels to critical darlings and popular favorites. These were not normal times. In previous years things were much more patchy. Balatro , 2024's indie nominee, was a massive viral hit. There was no indie nominee in 2023. In 2022, the lucky game was the distinctly slick and mainstream Stray . Prior to that, one indie game would typically break through every other year.

Increasing recognition of indie games among the critical community has been counterbalanced by the international expansion of The Game Awards jury . This expansion has tended to flatten the jury's taste , and tends to disadvantage indie developers who can't afford localization into multiple languages — not an issue for 2025's three big beasts.

So we turn to the 2026 race. There have been some superb and well-reviewed indie games this year, as there are every year: Big Walk , Mina the Hollower , Zero Parades , Mewgenics , Cairn , Denshattack! , Mixtape . None of them have been hits on the scale of the last few indie nominees, however, nor have they penetrated the culture in the same way as 2025’s games.

Image: Yacht Club Games Nevertheless, a nomination for one of them is still in prospect, because this year's GOTY slate is relatively weak , with many evenly matched titles fighting over the few nomination slots left after dead certs Grand Theft Auto 6 , The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , and Resident Evil Requiem are accounted for. In those circumstances, there's a path to nomination for an indie game with a stellar critical reputation and strong support.

The best candidates are Mina the Hollower and Big Walk , both critical darlings with 90-plus ratings on Metacritic. Mina was more widely covered at launch, but didn't click with a big audience. As a multiplayer co-op game, Big Walk has had a longer tail in the conversation, and has more viral stickiness. Jury members have probably been playing it over time with their friend groups. It's been my pick of the two so far, and its case was buoyed by a win in the Critic's Choice category at this week's Golden Joystick Awards .

However, also this week, developer House House made the disastrous admission that generative AI had been used to write some code for Big Walk . This will likely rule the game out of contention for several indie awards, like the IGF and Indie Game Awards. (The Indie Game Awards stripped Clair Obscur of its 2025 Game of the Year award over use of generative AI.) Its impact on Big Walk 's fortunes at The Game Awards is less clear.

Image: House House/Panic The broad-church Game Awards jury is likely less swayed by ethical issues such as AI usage than small, indie-specialist juries. That said, Big Walk will need the whole indie-fan coalition within The Game Awards jury to rally around it if it's going to get a nomination. An added wrinkle is that the AI news hit toward the final stage of The Game Awards' two-step nomination process. Jury members offended by the AI usage would have to actively remove Big Walk nominations they'd already made, rather than just not make them.

The controversy might not hurt Big Walk 's chances as much as you might think, But it certainly doesn't help them. In a tight race for those final nominations, the leading indie contender just took a big knock. Can Mina the Hollower take up the mantle? Or will Big Walk 's loss be some AAA title's gain — Control Resonant , perhaps, or 007 First Light ? We'll find out soon enough.

What’s in pole position for gaming’s top prize? Let’s make some predictions

items.title: Former BioWare lead says new Mass Effect could be made for ‘well under 200 million’
items.summary: The former lead dev says $200 million would be ‘more than enough’ for Mass Effect…
items.content:
The former lead dev says $200 million would be ‘more than enough’ for Mass Effect

Video Game News 11th Nov 2026 / 3:07 pm Posted by Rhiannon Bevan A former lead designer at BioWare says that a new Mass Effect game could be made for “well under 200 million”.

This claim comes from Christina Norman, who was with BioWare [219 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/companies/electronic-arts/bioware/ >BioWare from 2005 to 2011, working on the first three Mass Effect games. She made this comment in response to the news that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 [75 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/clair-obscur-expedition-33/ >Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 cost $10 million to develop.

“This is a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million,” says Norman. “5x the budget of Clair Obscure: Expedition 33 should be more than enough.

“You can always spend more, but clever small teams can get it done.”

If true, this would make the new Mass Effect cheaper to develop than recent titles like Cyberpunk 2077 [561 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/cyberpunk-2077/ >Cyberpunk 2077 , Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 [221 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/marvels-spider-man-2/ >Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 , and The Last of Us Part 2 [316 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/the-last-of-us-part-2/ >The Last of Us Part 2 , and even older releases such as Halo 2 and Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2 [213 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/call-of-duty/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-2/ >Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009), when adjusted for inflation.

It would, however, be the most expensive Mass Effect game ever made. Mass Effect: Andromeda has the highest budget of them all, costing a reported $100 million to develop. Since then, development costs for most triple-A games have ballooned much higher than this.

Norman’s comments come as fans mobilise to save the Mass Effect and Dragon Age series, following Electronic Arts [1,957 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/companies/electronic-arts/ >EA ‘s decision to shutter BioWare. The studio closure resulted in the cancellation of a fifth Mass Effect game, Mass Effect Universe, which had a trailer ready to go .

BioWare co-founder Trent Oster has since expressed his interest in trying to acquire BioWare’s IPs from EA , and has even suggested bringing the team back together to work on them. James Ohlen, who worked on the first two Baldur’s Gate games, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and Dragon Age: Origins, has said he’d like to join him.

Assuming the duo could get their hands on the rights to Mass Effect again, getting the funding for a game would be another matter, as many developers are struggling to secure investors. With that said, a petition to save Mass Effect has 325,605 signatures at the time of writing, so the interest is clearly there.

items.title: Mass Effect Could Still Be Saved, Ex-BioWare Developer Suggests, With Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Holding the Key
items.summary: The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.
items.content:
The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.

In the days since EA announced it was shutting down its storied RPG game studio and killing its in-development Mass Effect Universe project, discussion has turned to the costs behind creating another AAA-budget entry in BioWare's space opera series, following a report that EA decided to invest in Star Wars instead .

Last week, BioWare co-founder Trent Oster suggested that EA would likely have been on the hook for at least $200 million in development costs to finish Mass Effect Universe at a level that fans expected.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200m+," Oster wrote on X/Twitter. "That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work." (To be fair, there is still that Mass Effect TV series in the works. And there certainly won't be any bigger plan in place for the IP if its flagship next game is cancelled.)

Now, Mass Effect lead programmer Christina Norman has said the game could be made for around $50 million — a figure that is five times the budget spent by the makers of Clair Obscur.

Highlighting a report on the French-made RPG's overall budget, which was pegged at less than $10 million, Norman wrote on X/Twitter that this was "a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million.

"I mean 5x the budget of Claire obscure expedition 33 should be more than enough," she continued. "You can always spend more but clever small teams can get it done."

Norman spent more than six years at BioWare working on the original Mass Effect trilogy, firstly as a lead programmer responsible for creating the franchise's conversation system, before moving on to become lead designer for Mass Effect 2 and 3, working to improve the series' gameplay.

In the years since, Norman served stints at Riot Games and her own co-founded startup, before becoming a full-time machine learning engineering consultant focused on LLM-directed character conversations. Still, there's no suggestion that LLM technology would be needed to turn in Mass Effect Universe on a smaller budget.

Even Oster has said he believed a new Mass Effect could be made for "cheaper" than $200m, though it "wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept," he wrote in a follow-up post. Alas, Oster also highlighted another big blocker to a new Mass Effect being made — that EA still owns the franchise's rights, and may never want to give them up, even if it's not actively using them. "The big push would be getting the IP free," he concluded. "The fans deserve more."

Last week's annual N7 Day celebration of the Mass Effect franchise featured the Normandy's cast and crew teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect . This followed an array of footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect Universe appearing online, and a petition for EA to reconsider its decision which has gained more than 325,000 signatures . A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 | Dev Blog - Photo Mode
items.summary: Expeditioners, We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!! We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts invol
items.content:
Expeditioners,

We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!!

We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts involved in getting the Photo Mode set up, so we thought we’d show a bit of the process in this blog and talk a bit about what went into building this feature.

There were a few key people involved in the development of this, and each of them had a part to write here !

VINCENT CONSTANTIN-TURKI – Producer \

One of the main features we wanted to introduce with the Thank You Update was Photo Mode. It felt like a meaningful way to give something back to the players and thank them for their commitment to the game.

What’s funny is that the team in charge of developing Photo Mode doesn’t usually use this feature in other games, which is why we decided to collaborate with Shinobi. He helped us design a Photo Mode that would truly resonate with players.

NAJA DALMAGNE – QA Coordinator \

In many games we tested, Photo Modes often felt restrictive, which could quickly become frustrating. So, from the very beginning, one of the key goals we all agreed on was to give players as much freedom as possible. It was really about letting players express their creativity without getting in the way.

During development, the QA team ran into some unexpected and sometimes quite funny issues. One of the funniest, but also one of the most severe, involved characters whose heads or torsos could become displaced or deformed when opening the Photo Mode if they hadn’t been visible on screen for a while during exploration.

One feature I’m particularly proud of is the lighting system Florian worked on. It offers great flexibility while remaining fairly easy to use, which really makes a difference when you're trying to get the perfect shot.

FLORIAN TORRES – Senior Gameplay Programmer \ \

I love giving players as many tools and features as possible (that’s literally the purpose of my job).

When we started working on the photo mode, our goal was to give players as few restrictions as possible and that’s what I was in charge of coding: infinite camera distance, the ability to pass through collisions, lots of customizable lights, many (weird) filters, and more.

Of course, that comes with its challenges, but in the end it allows players to see a lot of things we don’t want to show during normal gameplay. The photo mode became a way to peek behind the scenes of each cinematic or environment, and sometimes even see how we have created the entire game.

Ever wondered what happens outside the camera frame? Here’s an example (sorry cinematic team, I love you).

LUDOVIC ‘SHINOBI’ HELME – Photo Mode Consultant \

We felt it was important to include anything that increases the “freedom” factor for players. It opens up countless possibilities every time someone enters photo mode: a very generous camera range to capture unseen details or create epic compositions, RGB curves control to edit and build your own color schemes, a strong custom lighting system to truly take ownership of a scene, and solid depth-of-field management.

But when all of that is also available in cutscenes - giving access to those incredible facial expressions and emotions - that’s when I really start to feel satisfied.

Every shot I’ve seen has blown my mind, and I often wish I’d been the one to come up with the idea. It’s truly inspiring.

I’m very proud that the team managed to create a tool that is both beginner-friendly and deeply satisfying for more experienced photographers. Finding that balance is extremely difficult.

With all of these features, there had to be a user-friendly way for people to make use of everything. Making sure players had full control of all the settings and could navigate all the features comes down to our awesome Gameplay & UI Programmer, VICTOR BOULEZ.

Thank you for all of your appreciation and feedback on this feature, we had a lot of fun making it and even more fun watching you use it!

This past week, especially, we’ve really loved the work you’ve all been putting into the social Photo Mode Prompt Challenge!! We’ve seen some amazing photography this past week, it’s completely blown our minds how creative you have been able to get with the prompts and tools.

Even though the challenge is over, feel free to keep sharing your work with us on social media, we thoroughly enjoy seeing some of your masterpieces!!

In the meantime, we are continuing to work on fixes for ongoing problems, keep an eye on the bug thread and socials to stay updated on the latest.

Finally, we leave you with some of our favourite uses of photo mode.

items.title: I played Cory in the House for Nintendo DS to find out if it’s truly better than Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: I played the Disney game threatening Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s top Metacritic ranking — is it actually good?
items.content:
a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Future / Nintendo / Disney / Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Threads Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Cory in the House for the Nintendo DS. That’s a name I haven’t heard in a long time. See, this 2008-released ‘adventure stealth’ game – as well as the TV show it’s based on – has been a meme for more than a decade. In the past, I’d often see Cory in the House being described as the ‘best anime of all time’. I’d also read Amazon reviews of the video game, which would hail it as a true ‘masterpiece’.

And now, in 2026, the meme seems to have been reborn. Users have taken to Metacritic and flooded it with positive reviews for Cory in the House on the Nintendo DS. And now, its user score sits at 9.3, which is indicative of ‘universal acclaim’. That score is so high, in fact, that the title is genuinely posing a threat to the top-ranked game on Metacritic by user score. And that game is none other than TechRadar’s Game of the Year of 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

After hearing all of this, you may be wondering: is Cory in the House on Nintendo DS actually good? Well, it’s your lucky day. See, back in my teens, a friend of mine jokingly gifted me the game for Christmas, and thankfully, I still own it to this day. So, I dusted the cartridge off, put it in my Nintendo 3DS console, and played through it for the very first time. Here’s what I made of my time with the ‘universally acclaimed’ title.

My game card didn’t work at first, but after a few blows and re-insertions, I was finally in. When I reached the main menu, there were a few options to choose from, including Story, an arcade mode, and a gallery. I got straight into the Story mode, and well…it was quite something.

In this campaign, you play as Cory Baxter, a teenager whose dad works as the head chef at The White House. As an aspiring businessman, Cory decides to sell bobbleheads of the President to the people of Washington DC – but trouble is afoot. See, an evil toymaker has turned the bobbleheads into hypnotic devices, and it’s your job to foil their malign scheme. Ridiculous? Absolutely. But I came into this experience with an open heart and an open mind.

I wasn't convinced by Elden Ring Tarnished Edition until I played it on Nintendo Switch 2 Final Fantasy Resonance review: classic RPG greatness made for 2026 Dark Souls is nothing compared to this: I wasn’t expecting a Mii to push me to my limits in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, but this one boss battle had me absolutely raging However, as soon as I got into the game, I was instantly struck by frankly horrifying visuals. No, really, I have a feeling Cory’s face will be haunting my nightmares for the foreseeable future. See, characters are so unrefined and blurred that you can’t even see their eyes or expressions. And that’s not inherent to the console – plenty of DS games pulled off nice-looking character models in spite of the handheld’s technical limitations.

Anyway, that’s not the end of the world, at least the gameplay could still be fun! Right? Well, I suppose in a sense, Cory in the House truly is a genre-defining title; in that it defines exactly how not to make an adventure stealth game. Movement is janky, throwing exploding fictional pastries is, somehow, totally mind-numbing, and the various settings are unbelievably bland. You play the occasional mini-game to progress the story, but even these are so laughably basic that I can’t even imagine a child having fun.

Oh, and one more thing. You have a lot of conversations with characters like Cory’s father, bandmates, and store workers – many of which are intended to be funny…at least I think they are? Sometimes I was unsure whether Cory was trying to crack a joke, but luckily, a laugh track would play when it was time for me to giggle. Artificial laughs even seem to play when characters don’t say anything remotely funny, which in itself was actually kinda entertaining. So, I guess there’s that?

So, there you have it, folks. Cory in the House for the Nintendo DS is – in spite of its 9.3 user score on Metacritic – a pretty terrible TV show tie-in, and it’s no wonder that its two critic review scores are listed as a 30 and a 40. Ouch.

Still, I’ve been finding the explosion of ironic meme-fuelled positive reviews pretty funny, even as a massive lover of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . And while we’re here, it only seems right to recommend this actual masterpiece to anyone who hasn’t tried it yet.

Tales of Eternia Remastered review: a real blast from the past After parting ways with Xbox, I pray that Double Fine is working on more games like Psychonauts 2 — one of the best platformers since Super Mario Odyssey Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave review: the best game on Nintendo Switch 2 so far Yes, Expedition 33 is a phenomenal RPG, with one of the best stories that’s ever been told through the video game medium, in my view. It plates up incredibly addictive gameplay, with an excellent parrying mechanic that’s a joy to master.
